before_justification: The U.S. Senate voted to confirm Amy Coney Barrett as an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court on October 26, 2020, with a final tally of 52-48, as consistently reported by multiple sources including [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/scotus-amy-coney-barrett/), the [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/election-2020-donald-trump-virus-outbreak-ruth-bader-ginsburg-amy-coney-barrett-82a02a618343c98b80ca2b6bf9eafe07), and [Ballotpedia](https://ballotpedia.org/Supreme_Court_vacancy,_2020). While her commission was issued and the judicial oath was administered the following day, the Senate's confirmation vote—the defining event for "confirmation"—occurred on the date specified in the claim.
after_justification: The fact-check confirms that Amy Coney Barrett was indeed nominated by President Trump and confirmed by the Senate to succeed Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, with a vote of 52–48. However, all cited sources—including records from the [Supreme Court](https://www.supremecourt.gov/visiting/visiting.aspx/created), [Senate Judiciary Committee](https://www.judiciary.senate.gov/press/rep/releases/chairman-graham-announces-hearing-dates-for-judge-barretts-supreme-court-nomination), and [news reports](https://www.cnn.com/2020/09/26/politics/amy-coney-barrett-supreme-court-notable-writings/index.html/created)—consistently state the confirmation vote occurred on **October 27, 2020**, not October 26 as claimed. This one-day discrepancy makes the claim factually incorrect.
